builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Factorized Context Attention: From Emulated to Native Grid Probing
summary: Factorized Context Attention replaces grid probing's repeated per-span re-encoding with a native block-sparse attention pass that encodes the input once into a shared KV cache and reads all local and strided spans in one batched forward. It costs a custom attention implementation with masking plus a stair position schedule, rather than any training or extra parameters. It can fail where the block-sparse pattern is unsupported by the reader's inference stack, where spans straddle the trained position range despite the schedule, or where tasks need dense cross-span interactions that strided probing misses.
rationale: FCA is training-free and works on frozen models the reader already runs, but gains depend on reimplementing block-sparse attention and validating accuracy on the reader's specific long-context workloads.

claims.statement: Factorized Context Attention replaces grid probing's repeated per-span re-encoding with a native block-sparse attention pass that encodes the input once into a shared KV cache and reads all local and strided spans in one batched forward. It costs a custom attention implementation with masking plus a stair position schedule, rather than any training or extra parameters. It can fail where the block-sparse pattern is unsupported by the reader's inference stack, where spans straddle the trained position range despite the schedule, or where tasks need dense cross-span interactions that strided probing misses.

Answers a subsequent question about the same input in as little as one tenth of the time of grid probing; also gains about 10 points over single-pass inference on long video and 9-14 points on long novels, retrieving needles at 4x the context window.
